title: Pileus
description:
The cap of a basidiomycete fruiting body — the visible top surface borne on a stipe (or sometimes sessile). Mycological treatments typically characterize the pileus along five axes: size (one or two diameter measurements), shape (often progressing with age), surface texture, color, and underlying context (flesh visible at a cut surface). This schema is the hand-authored Phase 1 seed; later phases replace it with corpus-induced versions via Pass A.

Worked example: Aureoboletus miniatoaurantiacus (taxon_0029f1413f69fd6d270f11e5aa0f806d3ba8687c0c1a5826330988ca90c02c06 in skol_exp_production_v4_02_00_treatments_prose). Pileus block: "Pileus 2.6–8 cm diam, subhemispherical when young, then convex to applanate; surface tomentose or pulverous, slightly wrinkled, yellowish orange to orange; context white, unchanging in colour when injured."

size_mm.description: Pileus diameter range in millimeters (mycologists report in cm or mm; we canonicalize to mm). Typically a min/max pair; some species add a parenthetical max_observed for rare outliers ("Pileus 38–75(–120) mm" → min=38, max=75, max_observed=120). Aureoboletus example: "Pileus 2.6–8 cm diam" → {min: 26, max: 80}.

min.description: Lower bound of the typical range, mm.

max.description: Upper bound of the typical range, mm. Must be ≥ min.

min_observed.description: Optional. Smaller than min, recorded as a rare outlier (parenthetical-extension form: "(2–)3–8 cm").

max_observed.description: Optional. Larger than max, recorded as a rare outlier.

shape.description: One or more shape descriptors. When more than one, the list is ordered by age progression (young → mature → old). Aureoboletus example: "subhemispherical when young, then convex to applanate" → ["subhemispherical", "convex", "applanate"]. Free text — the controlled vocabulary will be induced in a later phase; for now the values are whatever the source text uses.

surface_texture.description: Texture as observed by hand/lens. Often multiple descriptors are combined: "tomentose or pulverous, slightly wrinkled" → ["tomentose", "pulverous", "wrinkled"]. Common single-state values: glabrous (smooth), tomentose (felty), pulverous (powdery), squamulose (small scales), squamose (scales), viscid (sticky), velutinous (velvety), wrinkled, polished, dry. Free text in Phase 1; controlled-vocabulary induction is later.

color.description: Pileus surface color, given as the descriptive text from the treatment. Often a range ("pale yellowish at first but gradually darkening to dull tan"), sometimes accompanied by Munsell or hex codes in detailed treatments. Aureoboletus example: "yellowish orange to orange". Free text in Phase 1.
examples: pale yellowish at first but gradually darkening to dull tan

context_color.description: Color of the pileus context (the flesh just under the surface), as seen at a cut. May differ from the surface color. Aureoboletus example: "context white" → "white". Free text in Phase 1.

context_change_on_injury.description: How the pileus context changes color when cut or bruised. Diagnostic for many genera (Boletus stains blue; Lactarius exudes milk of various colors). Common single-state values: "unchanging", "staining blue", "staining red", "staining brown", "milky white", "milky orange". Free text in Phase 1.
